nodes.description: The terminal cytoband 3p26.3 carries three consecutive genes for closely related neuronal immunoglobulin cell adhesion molecules - CHL1, CNTN6 and CNTN4 - and is the region most frequently involved in chromosome 3p copy number variants. This branch is separable from the 3p25.3 core: deletions confined to it produce a milder, sometimes non-penetrant picture rather than the full syndrome.

nodes.description: Congenital heart disease in 3p- syndrome tracks with how far proximally the deletion extends, and microarray mapping refined a candidate cardiac susceptibility interval to roughly 200 kb - a region distinct from the neurodevelopmental critical interval. The gene has not been identified. CAV3 has been raised as a positional candidate in individual cases, but the entry does not assert it: the strongest such report reaches CAV3 by proximity and in silico reasoning after a karyotype that could not resolve the breakpoint.

nodes.description: Loss of one copy of the 3p25.3 interval that carries the neurodevelopmental core. Two genes in it have independent support. SETD5 sits inside the minimal 124 kb region shared by the smallest interstitial deletions, and SRGAP3 sits inside the roughly 1 Mb interval that microarray mapping assigned to the cognitive phenotype. The entry keeps both rather than choosing, because the two claims were made on different evidence and neither displaces the other.

nodes.description: The lesion is a heterozygous deletion of distal 3p, classically terminal with a breakpoint at or near 3p25 and extending to the telomere, though interstitial deletions lying wholly inside that interval reproduce the syndrome. Deletion size in cytogenetically detectable cases runs from roughly 6 to 12 Mb, and molecularly characterised interstitial cases go down to about 1 Mb. Breakpoints are not recurrent, which is the structural fact behind the entry's multi-gene model: different patients lose different combinations of the dosage-sensitive genes in the interval.

nodes.description: Reduced dosage of the 3p26.3 IgCAMs is expected to degrade neuritogenesis, axon guidance and synaptic function. The in vitro evidence for this is considerably stronger than the in vivo evidence: single-gene mouse knockouts do not reproduce the defects seen in culture, which the cited review attributes to compensation among the family members. That mismatch is recorded as a discussion rather than smoothed over here.

nodes.description:
BRPF1 sits at 3p25.3 immediately adjacent to SETD5 and is lost in the larger deletions. It is a chromatin regulator that scaffolds the MOZ, MORF and HBO1 acetyltransferases and is required for acetylation of histone H3 at lysine 23. The cited source proposes this branch as a third contributor to the neurodevelopmental and dysmorphic phenotype, and specifically to ptosis through a role in craniofacial development.
This node is deliberately weaker than the SETD5 and SRGAP3 branches beside it. The source hedges every causal statement it makes about BRPF1 ("may lead to", "can cause"), and its own patient analysis attributes only intellectual disability and ptosis to the BRPF1 deletion while explicitly excluding the hearing, renal and gastrointestinal features. The edges below are graded to match that hedging rather than to assert more than the source does.

nodes.description: SETD5 encodes a predicted SET-domain methyltransferase acting on chromatin. Truncating alleles trigger nonsense-mediated decay, so a deletion and an intragenic loss-of-function variant converge on the same halved dose. The binding here is deliberately the broad chromatin-organization process rather than a specific histone-methylation term: the cited work calls SETD5 a predicted methyltransferase and infers the SET domain in silico, so a narrower catalytic term would assert more than the sources do.

evidence.snippet: In silico domain prediction of SETD5, a predicted SET domain-containing histone methyltransferase (HMT), substantiated the presence of a SET domain and identified a novel putative PHD domain, strengthening a functional link to well-known histone-modifying ID genes.

nodes.description: SRGAP3 (MEGAP/srGAP3) is a Rho-family GTPase-activating protein expressed predominantly in fetal and adult brain, concentrated in hippocampus and cortex, and acting as a Rac1 GAP within the Slit-Robo pathway that guides neuronal migration and axonal branching. Halving its dose is proposed to disturb the neuronal architecture on which cognition depends.
